answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly. Agents must lock an opal stake to transact: every fake identity needs its own locked stake, so attack cost grows per forgery while honest agents pay once. New identities start with zero trust and must earn standing through a yarrow record of verified work before handling large transactions. Finally, a beacon challenge lets established agents flag suspicious newcomers, slashing the stake of any identity caught cheating. The attacker pays capital per identity, time building fake history, and risks losing the stake.
